title: How Security Camera Night Vision Works in 60 Seconds 🌙📷 #shorts
description:
Security cameras see in total darkness by lighting the scene with infrared light our eyes can't see. A light sensor notices dusk, a tiny IR-cut filter slides away, and a ring of infrared LEDs floods the area, so the sensor records a black-and-white image. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#nightvision #securitycamera #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Security cameras see in *total darkness* by using light your eyes *can't see*.

steps.label: Dusk
steps.text: A small *light sensor* on the front notices when the sun goes down.

steps.label: Filter
steps.text: A tiny *IR-cut filter* slides away from the sensor with a quiet *click*.

steps.label: LEDs
steps.text: A ring of *infrared LEDs* switches on and floods the scene with invisible light.

steps.label: Bounce
steps.text: That light *bounces* off objects and back into the lens to the *image sensor*.

steps.label: B&W
steps.text: Infrared carries no color, so the picture turns *black and white*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Sense, switch, *illuminate*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
